newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: FISCHER BLAMES EXPORT DROP ON LABOR
Trade Minister Tim Fischer says Australia's 12-billion dollar drop in exports to Asia is the fault of the former government.
This follows a report from the Australian National University showing Australia's share of the market in East Asia fell from just over 4 percent in 1993 to below 3 percent in 1995.
The report says the drop equals about 12-billion dollars in lost exports.
Mr Fischer says Labor provided little incentive for the Australian economy to adjust to the changing nature of demand in East Asia.
He says Labor's policies left Australia behind when it came to keeping up with the rest of the world in diversifying and remaining competitive.
MAN LEAVES AFTER QUESTIONING ON BONDI BASHING
A man has left a police station after more than three hours of questioning over the fatal bashing of English tourist Brian Hagland at Bondi Beach in Sydney.
Police say the man entered a police station this morning and assisted police with their inquiries.
Mr Hagland's body has been released, following a second post-mortem that found no further major injuries.
His girlfriend, Connie Casey, is preparing to return to England for the funeral.
OPTUS STOP WORK ON SACRED SITE
Talks have been arranged to resolve a problem between Optus and a the Aboriginal Areas Protection Authority in the Northern Territory over the erection of a telecommunications tower.
Optus was forced to stop work on the tower at Heavitree Gap near Alice Springs after failing to get clearance to work on the site.
The Aboriginal Areas Protection Authority's Michael Pickering told ABC Radio that work on the tower, has damaged a highly significant site in the local sacred landscape.
He says an amicable resolution to the problem is being sought.
BY-ELECTION DATE SET
The by-election for the Federal seat of Lindsay will be held on October 19th.
The High Court has ordered the fresh election for the seat in outer western Sydney because Liberal Jackie Kelly, who won the seat in the March election, was ineligible to be a candidate.
Acting Speaker, Gary Nehl, issued the writ for the election today.
The electoral rolls will close next Monday, and nominations will close the following Friday.
DALAI LAMA ENCOURAGES BUDDHIST EXCHANGES
The Dalai Lama says it's an important international step towards peace for Buddhists from different traditions to exchange experiences, like Australian Buddhists did yesterday.
The exiled spiritual leader of Tibet says in the past Buddhists from different traditons have come together in India and America, and more such exchanges are needed.
His Holiness says Buddhist teachings and his public address later today are relevant for all people not just Tibetan Buddhists.
HARRADINE RUBBISHES DEAL CLAIM

Tasmanian Independent Senator, Brian Harradine, says he has asked for Medicare-funded abortions to be stopped but it's not part of a deal with the Government over the part-sale of Telstra. He says that suggestion is absolutely fanciful.

Senator Harradine says he raised ending Medicare-funded abortions, and assistance for family planning clinics along with other proposals in a pre-budget meeting with the Prime Minister. But he strongly denies he made his support of the Telstra sale contingent on them being acted upon.
The Government needs Senator Harradine's vote to get the Telstra sale through Parliament.
